newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm Council approves various measures for 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Farm Council approves various measures for 1997/98.

text.p: Austria won extra aid for durum wheat producers as part of the European Union's 1997/98 farm price package, Austrian diplomats said on Thursday.

Farmers in the Pannonia region, east of Vienna, who have traditionally grown durum wheat, will be entitled to aid of 358.6 ecus per hectare, instead of 138.9 ecus, under the 1997/98 EU farm price package agreed in Luxembourg on Wednesday.
But the durum wheat area eligible for the aid remains at 5,000 hectares.
The European Union's standard beef intervention price will remain at 347.5 ecus per 100 kg carcasse weight in 1997/98 (July/June), the EU said in a statement.
EU farm ministers also requested the European Commission to urgently examine steps to ensure that the intervention system stops a downward spiral in prices.
The request follows concern from Ireland and other major beef producers.
European Union milk, butter and skimmed milk prices will remain unchanged in 1997/98 (July/June), the statement added.
The target price for milk stays at 309.8 ecus per tonne and intervention prices for butter and skimmed milk powder at 3,282 ecus and 2,055.2 ecus per tonne respectively
Finland and Sweden's exemptions on milk fat content were extended for two years until December 31, 1999.
The European Commission was requested to propose a two year extension of special measures for east German states if no solution could be found for their milk quota problems.
The Commission was also asked to consider more flexible milk quota measures for Italian and Spanish producers.
Farm ministers unanimously agreed to allow Italy to pay off 100 million ecu debts of 348 bankrupt farm cooperatives, EU officials said.
Unanimous agreement was needed to override the European Commission's objections to the move.
The Commission argued that the Italian goverment's plan to pay off the debts over 10 years was against EU state aid rules.
